title: Why Your Own Touch Often Feels Less Ticklish
titleSupport: Conditional title only if live Page composer provides field
description:
Why is someone else's touch often ticklier than your own?

Your nervous system can predict some sensations produced by your movements, making self-touch feel weaker. It does not simply erase the touch.

Light-touch experiments provide an important clue. Laughter-inducing tickling is harder to explain, people differ, and a light tickly sensation can be self-made.

Original illustrative animation; prediction metaphor, not neural recordings. Synthetic narration; original synthesized sound.

Research: Blakemore et al. (1998); Kilteni & Ehrsson (2022); Kilteni et al. (2019); Proelss et al. (2022); Kilteni (2025 review).
